headings.title: Recording results and voter-approved bond execution and levy
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Requires recording the election result and, upon approval by the constitutionally required voter percentage, directs commissioners to execute the bonds and provide a direct annual property tax levy sufficient to pay principal and interest as due. Revised title during review to preserve voter-approval condition.

headings.title: Ballot form for road and bridge bonds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 (including indented ballot block) and history notes. Sets the substantial ballot question form for issuing special road district road and bridge bonds.

headings.title: Minimum sale price, warrant disbursement, and permitted uses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history notes. Prohibits selling bonds below 95% of par value, requires deposit with the county treasurer and warrant disbursement signed by the president or vice president and attested by the secretary, and restricts proceeds to election costs and district bridge, culvert, and public road work.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived version (5 subsections, including indented ballot form) and history/prior-revision notes (RSMo 1939 § 8717 through A.L. 1990 H.B. 1621); verified source identity and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Checked 5% assessed-valuation bond limit, denominations, legal interest cap, 20-year maturity, election notice, conditional bond execution and direct annual tax levy upon constitutionally required voter approval, ballot form, 95% par minimum, county treasurer disbursement, and restricted uses. Revised subsection 3 title to preserve voter-approval condition; retained subsections 1, 2, 4, and 5.

headings.title: Landowner improvement petition and preparation of plans and estimate
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 8718). Covers petitions by owners of a majority of district acres within one-half mile of a public road requesting permanent improvement assessed against all district lands (stating endpoints, improvement type, and up to 15 installments), requiring commissioners to prepare a district map, road profile, plans and specifications, and cost estimate.

headings.title: State highway engineer review and approval of plans
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Requires submitting the map, profile, plans, specifications, and cost estimate to the state highway engineer to approve, revise, or prepare acceptable plans and estimate and return them to the commissioners.

headings.title: Land valuation, distance classifications, and tie-breaking average
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Requires commissioners to value each tract independent of buildings, list tracts by distance bands from the road (within 0.5, 0.5–1, 1–1.5, and over 1.5 miles), and average the three commissioners' valuations if they cannot agree on a tract.

headings.title: Certification, county clerk filing, and published hearing notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history notes. Requires commissioners to certify and acknowledge the land list like deeds and file it with the petition, map, profile, plans, specifications, and estimate with the county clerk, who must publish at least two weekly newspaper notices setting a county commission protest/objection hearing date at least two weeks after first publication.

headings.title: New notice when county commission is not in session
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history notes. Requires the county clerk to give a new notice setting another hearing day if the county commission fails for any cause to be in session on the noticed date.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived version (5 subsections) and history/prior-revision notes (RSMo 1939 § 8718); verified source identity and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Checked majority-acreage petition within one-half mile (up to 15 installments), map/profile/plans/estimate preparation, state highway engineer review, tract valuation independent of buildings and four distance bands with 3-commissioner tie-breaking average, acknowledged certification, two-week weekly newspaper hearing notice, and new notice if the county commission is not in session. Retained all five titles as accurate.

headings.title: Filing written landowner protests and objections before hearing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 8719). Permits owners of district land within one-half mile of the road to file signed written protests describing their land and acreage before the noticed hearing day, and permits anyone interested in district land to show why the road cannot be improved and charged against district lands.

headings.title: County commission consideration and prima facie petition effect
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Directs the county commission to consider the petition, filed protests, and reasons against the improvement on or after the noticed day, and makes the petition prima facie evidence of its allegations.

headings.title: Dismissal upon protest or bar and preparatory cost judgment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Requires the county commission, if owners of a majority of acres within one-half mile protest or sufficient reason is shown against the improvement, to ascertain commissioners' preparatory costs, dismiss the petition, and enter judgment against petitioners for costs including those expenses (cf. section 233.355(3), which lacks a cost-judgment clause). Revised title during review to preserve the protest/bar condition.

headings.title: Prerequisites for hearing land-list and valuation objections
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history notes. Directs the county commission, upon finding insufficient protests, no sufficient bar, lawful establishment of the road, and proper sections 233.170 to 233.315 clerk notice, to hear land-list and valuation objections and exceptions, with authority to continue the hearing as justice requires.

headings.title: Valuation approval, cost findings, special tax order, and installments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history notes. Covers modifying and approving the land list and valuations with clerk certification, finding estimated improvement, preparatory, petitioner attorney's fee, and incidental costs, ordering a special tax for the aggregate plus 10% for emergencies, ordering the improvement per filed plans, and stating the petitioned installment count.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived version (5 subsections) and history/prior-revision notes (RSMo 1939 § 8719); verified source identity and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Checked one-half-mile written landowner protests and interested-party objections, prima facie petition effect, conditional dismissal with preparatory-cost judgment against petitioners (contrasted with section 233.355(3), which omits the cost-judgment clause and combines dismissal with valuation hearing), prerequisites for valuation hearings under sections 233.170 to 233.315, and special tax order plus 10% emergency margin. Revised subsection 3 title to make the protest/bar condition explicit; retained subsections 1, 2, 4, and 5.

headings.title: Single-installment special tax bills and required contents
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 8721). Requires the county clerk, when a special tax is ordered payable in one installment, to make out a separate numbered special tax bill per tract in favor of the district stating the order date, tract description, and assessed amount, signed by the district president or vice president and attested by the county clerk.

headings.title: Record book, publication notice, lien priority, and delinquency interest
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Covers recording tax-bill abstracts, depositing bills with the county treasurer, one-time newspaper notice, establishing a paramount lien (inferior only to general state, county, school, and road taxes) covering collection costs and commission-fixed attorney's fees, and imposing 8% annual interest on bills unpaid after thirty days.

headings.title: County treasurer payment collection, cancellation, and clerk notation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Directs the county treasurer to receive and record tax-bill payments, cancel paid bills, and credit principal and interest separately on a special district account, and requires the county clerk to note payment in the record book upon exhibition or report.

headings.title: Commissioner borrowing against unpaid single-installment tax bills
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history notes. Authorizes commissioners, if bills remain unpaid after thirty days, to borrow up to the unpaid aggregate at not over 8% interest, repayable solely via warrants from collections of those unpaid bills (with no other district or commissioner obligation), and requires depositing borrowed money with the county treasurer.

headings.title: Lien foreclosure suits, prima facie evidence, and attorney's fees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history notes. Permits foreclosure suits after six months unpaid and requires them after twelve months in circuit court with the district as plaintiff, makes each tax bill prima facie evidence of a valid lien, and taxes a court-fixed reasonable attorney's fee as costs.

headings.title: Restricted uses of tax-bill collections, borrowed funds, and interest
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history notes. Restricts special tax-bill collections, borrowed money, and depositary interest to preparatory expenses, petitioner attorney's fees, road improvement costs, working/administrative/incidental expenses, and remaining balance for maintenance, subject to repaying any borrowed money with interest from collections on unpaid bills.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived version (6 subsections) and history/prior-revision notes (RSMo 1939 § 8721); verified source identity and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Checked single-installment special tax bill contents, clerk record book and county treasurer deposit, paramount lien with commission-fixed attorney's fee and 8% interest after 30 days, treasurer collection/cancellation, 8% non-recourse commissioner borrowing, circuit court foreclosure suits (permissive at 6 months, mandatory at 12 months) with court-fixed attorney's fee, and restricted fund uses. Retained all six titles as accurate.

headings.title: Equal multi-installment schedule and interest apportionment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 8722). Provides that when a special tax order recites a petition for multiple installments, the tax is payable in the petitioned number of equal installments (not exceeding fifteen) with interest apportioned against district lands by the same rule as principal.

headings.title: Installment due dates and six percent interest calculation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (including subdivisions (1)–(2)) and history notes. Establishes December 31 annual installment due dates and 6% annual interest accrual periods (through April 1) depending on whether the order is made January 1–October 31 or on or after November 1.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived version (2 subsections, including subdivisions (1)–(2)) and history/prior-revision notes (RSMo 1939 § 8722); verified source identity and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Checked equal multi-installment cap (15), proportionate interest apportionment, and December 31 due dates with 6% annual interest through April 1 differentiated by pre-November 1 versus November 1-or-later order dates. Retained both titles as accurate.

headings.title: County clerk special tax record book entries
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 8722). Requires the county clerk after the assessment order to procure a special tax record book and charge each tract on the commissioners' list with its special tax, interest charges, installment dates, and amounts.

headings.title: Installment tax bill issuance, lien priority, and monthly penalties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Requires delivering separate installment special tax bills to the county collector at least thirty days before due dates (excluding tracts paid in full), specifies bill contents, creates a paramount lien (except general taxes) including commission-fixed attorney's fees, and imposes a 2% delinquency penalty plus 2% monthly thereafter.

headings.title: County collector payment receipts, cancellation, and clerk notation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Requires the county collector to receive and record installment tax-bill payments and cancel paid bills, and requires the county clerk to note payment in the special tax record book upon exhibition or collector report.

headings.title: Remittance to county treasurer and special district accounting
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history notes. Requires the county collector to pay tax-bill collections to the county treasurer, who must credit the district on a special account distinguishing principal from interest and penalties.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived version (4 subsections) and history/prior-revision notes (RSMo 1939 § 8722); verified source identity and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Checked clerk special tax record book, 30-day advance delivery of installment bills to the county collector excluding tracts paid in full, paramount lien with county-commission-fixed attorney's fee (contrasted with court-fixed fee and omitted paid-in-full clause in section 233.380(2)), 2% delinquency and monthly penalties, collector payment/cancellation/clerk notation, and remittance to county treasurer with separate principal and interest/penalty accounting. headings.title: Landowner thirty-day election to pay in one installment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 8722). Permits a tract owner within thirty days after the assessment order to file a signed written election with the county clerk to pay the full special tax in one installment by the first installment due date, requiring clerk notation and delivery of a single-installment bill with interest to April 1 to the county collector.

headings.title: Liens, penalties, interest, and collection of single-installment bills
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Makes single-installment tax bills issued under subsection 1 constitute liens, bear penalties and interest, be collectible in the same manner, and otherwise conform to multi-installment tax-bill provisions.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived version (2 subsections) and history/prior-revision notes (RSMo 1939 § 8722); verified source identity and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Checked 30-day written landowner election to pay in one installment with interest to April 1, clerk notation and collector bill delivery, and parity of liens, penalties, interest, and collection with multi-installment tax bills. Retained both titles as accurate.

headings.title: Bond issuance limit, denominations, interest rate, and payment dates
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 8722). Directs commissioners after thirty days from the assessment order to issue special assessment bonds up to 90% of the ordered tax (net of tracts electing single-installment payment), in minimum $100 denominations at up to 6% interest payable April 1 and October 1.

headings.title: Bond maturity installments and designated place of payment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Requires bonds to be payable in the same number of installments (not necessarily equal) as the special tax, maturing April 1 after each tax installment, with principal and interest payable at a banking house or trust company named in the bonds.

headings.title: Bond execution, county clerk registration, and state auditor registration
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Requires signing by the road district president, attestation and book registration by the county clerk before delivery, and state auditor registration applying sections 108.240 to 108.300 to bonds issued under sections 233.170 to 233.315.

headings.title: County treasurer custody, security eligibility, and trust fund investment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history notes. Requires depositing state-registered bonds with the county treasurer until disposed of under sections 233.170 to 233.315, makes them eligible lawful securities like drainage/levee bonds under sections 242.010 to 242.690, 243.010 to 243.540, and 108.240 to 108.300, and authorizes county commissions to invest school or trust funds in them at par.

headings.title: Public or private bond sale and minimum price
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 8722). Authorizes road district commissioners to sell special assessment bonds at public or private sale for not less than 95% of face value.

headings.title: Payment sources, interest reserve requirement, and bond payment duty
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Limits bond collectibility to special tax bills, bond-sale proceeds, and county depositary interest; requires the county treasurer to hold an interest reserve covering upcoming interest before the next tax installment plus 3% of unmatured bond principal; and directs application of applicable funds to due and unpaid bonds and interest.

headings.title: Dedicated tax-bill use for bonds and surplus exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Dedicates all special tax-bill collections to paying bonds and interest, except surplus exceeding past-due bonds, upcoming bonds and interest before the next installment, and a 3% unmatured-principal reserve may be used for other authorized purposes.

headings.title: Bond delivery upon sale and cancellation upon payment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history notes. Directs the county treasurer to deliver sold bonds to purchasers upon commissioners' order and receipt of payment, and to cancel paid bonds and deliver them to the county clerk.

headings.title: Permitted uses of bond proceeds, surplus collections, and interest
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history notes. Restricts unreserved bond-sale proceeds, authorized surplus tax-bill collections, and excess depositary interest (disbursed by warrants) to preparatory costs, petitioner attorney's fees, road improvement costs per filed plans, working/administrative/incidental expenses, and remaining balance for maintenance.

Checked 95% minimum public/private bond sale price, limited payment sources and county treasurer interest plus 3% unmatured-principal reserve, dedicated tax-bill bond payment with surplus exception, delivery on sale and cancellation on payment to county clerk, and restricted uses of unreserved bond proceeds, surplus tax-bill collections, and excess interest. Retained all five titles as accurate.

headings.title: Partial payments without cancellation until paid in full
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 8724). Authorizes county treasurers and collectors to receive and receipt for partial payments on special tax bills while prohibiting cancellation until paid in full.

headings.title: Tax apportionment and separate bills for divided tracts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Requires the county commission, upon application of an owner who has divided or desires to divide a taxed tract, to apportion the special tax across the resulting tracts so subsequent special tax bills issue separately.

headings.title: Validity of tax bills with errors and clerk corrections
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Provides that sections 233.170 to 233.315 special tax bills are not void due to errors but remain valid for the proper amount and extent, and authorizes the county clerk to correct errors at any time.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived version (3 subsections) and history/prior-revision notes (RSMo 1939 § 8724); verified source identity and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Checked partial-payment receipting by county treasurers/collectors without premature cancellation, county commission apportionment for divided tracts, and validity/clerk error correction for sections 233.170 to 233.315 special tax bills. Retained all three titles as accurate.

headings.title: Written contract with lowest and best bidder, penalties, and bond
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 8725). Requires commissioners, after an improvement order, to enter a written district contract with the lowest and best bidder including a completion deadline, daily delay penalty, and board-approved contractor performance and labor/material payment bond. Revised title during review to restore exact statutory phrasing "lowest and best bidder".

headings.title: Bid advertising and commissioner conflict-of-interest prohibition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Allows commissioners to advertise for bids in any manner they choose, and prohibits letting the contract to any commissioner or allowing any commissioner direct or indirect pecuniary interest beyond official duties.

headings.title: Contract price cap and eighty percent progress-payment limit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Caps contract payment at the county commission's found estimated cost plus 10%, and prohibits paying over 80% of the value of work performed and materials furnished before entire completion.

headings.title: Warrants on county treasurer for contractor payments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history notes. Directs commissioners to draw warrants on the county treasurer as contractor payments become payable under contract terms.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived version (4 subsections) and history/prior-revision notes (RSMo 1939 § 8725); verified source identity and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Checked written contract with lowest and best bidder, completion deadline, daily delay penalty, performance and labor/material payment bond, discretionary bid advertising, commissioner pecuniary-interest prohibition, estimated-cost-plus-10% cap, 80% progress-payment limit, and county treasurer warrants. Revised subsection 1 title to restore exact statutory phrasing "lowest and best bidder"; retained subsections 2–4.

headings.title: County collector compensation for special tax bills
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 8728, A.L. 2012 H.B. 1037). Grants county collectors the same compensation for collecting sections 233.170 to 233.315 special tax bills as for collecting county taxes.

headings.title: County clerk fees for tax bills, records, and bonds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Sets itemized fees for county clerks under sections 233.170 to 233.315 (6 cents per tax bill issued/attested, 5 cents per abstract recorded, 4 cents per tract for installment tax records, 20 cents per bond attested/registered, and statutory or commission-fixed compensation for other services).

headings.title: Commissioner monthly compensation cap and expense reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes (A.L. 2012 H.B. 1037). Authorizes a majority of commissioners of sections 233.170 to 233.315 districts to fix commissioner compensation up to $100 per month (unchangeable during an elected or appointed term) in addition to reimbursing all district business expenses including reasonable attorney's fees.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived version (3 subsections) and history/prior-revision notes (RSMo 1939 § 8728, A.L. 2012 H.B. 1037); verified source identity and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Checked county collector compensation parity, itemized county clerk fees under sections 233.170 to 233.315, and commissioner compensation up to $100/month (fixed by board majority, unchangeable during term) plus business expenses and reasonable attorney's fees (contrasted with unpaid service in section 233.420(3)). Retained all three titles as accurate.

headings.title: Disincorporation by landowner acreage petition, notice, and hearing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 8731 through A.L. 2017 S.B. 112; catchline parenthetically notes Christian, Jasper and Barry counties). Authorizes a county commission, upon petition of owners of a majority of acres in a sections 233.170 to 233.315 district and four successive weeks' published newspaper notice prior to hearing, to disincorporate the district if in its opinion the public good will be advanced.

headings.title: Voter-petition dissolution election and ballot in qualifying counties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (including embedded HTML ballot table with YES/NO checkboxes) and notes. In qualifying counties (population >= 32,000 adjoining a first-classification county with a >= 100,000 city that adjoins no other first-classification county), requires the county clerk upon petition of 50 district registered voters to certify the dissolution ballot question and requires disincorporation upon majority vote.

headings.title: Eight-week filing deadline for subsection 2 petitions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Requires any petition filed under subsection 2 to be submitted to the county clerk no later than eight weeks before the next countywide election at which the question will be voted upon.

headings.title: Commission disincorporation by voter petition in qualifying first-classification counties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. In first-classification counties with 104,600–104,700 inhabitants, provides for presenting a dissolution petition signed by the lesser of 50 or a majority of district registered voters to the county commission, which must disincorporate the district after notice and hearing if it finds the public good advanced; excludes two-county districts.

headings.title: Commission disincorporation by voter petition in qualifying third-classification counties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and notes. In third-classification non-township counties with 34,000–34,100 inhabitants, provides for presenting a dissolution petition signed by the lesser of 50 or a majority of district registered voters to the county commission for disincorporation after notice, hearing, and public-good finding; excludes two-county districts.

headings.title: Commission disincorporation by voter petition in qualifying second-classification counties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and notes. In second-classification counties with 54,200–54,300 inhabitants, provides for presenting a dissolution petition signed by the lesser of 50 or a majority of district registered voters to the county commission for disincorporation after notice, hearing, and public-good finding; excludes two-county districts.

headings.title: Commission disincorporation by voter petition for single-county districts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and notes. Applies in any county (excluding two-county road districts), providing for presenting a dissolution petition signed by the lesser of 50 or a majority of district registered voters to the county commission for disincorporation after notice, hearing, and public-good finding.

headings.title: Commission disincorporation by voter petition for two-county districts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and notes. Governs disincorporating a two-county road district in any county by voter petitions (lesser of 50 or a majority of district registered voters in each county) to each county commission, requiring notice, hearing, public-good finding, and disincorporation in both counties before disincorporation takes effect.

headings.title: Combining single-county road districts by commissioner petition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 (including subdivisions (1)–(7)), history notes, and Revisor footnote (*Word "; and" appears in original rolls at end of subdivision (6)). Authorizes county commissions to consolidate two or more sections 233.170 to 233.315 districts upon petition by a majority of commissioners in each district, covering four-week notice, public hearing, order and effective date, initial staggered commissioners, vesting of assets/liabilities at the lower tax levy, transfer instruments, and exclusion of two-county districts.

headings.title: Election dissolution alternative for fourth-classification counties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2008 S.B. 896). Authorizes dissolving a special road district by election in lieu of section 233.290 or 233.295, limited exclusively to special road districts in fourth-classification counties.

headings.title: Voter petition, election order, and four-year waiting period
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires the county commission, upon petition of 50 registered voters of the district, to order submission of dissolution to voters, subject to a four-year waiting period from district establishment or the last expansion/dissolution election (retaining archived source duplication "make an order that the dissolution of the special road district order that the question...").

headings.title: Ballot form for special road district dissolution
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 (including indented ballot block) and history note. Sets the substantial ballot question form for dissolving a special road district under this section.

headings.title: Disincorporation upon majority vote
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Provides that upon a majority vote in favor of dissolution, the special road district is disincorporated and operation of the law ceases there.

headings.title: Preservation of bonds, levies, assessments, and unpaid parcel taxes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Preserves the validity of existing district bonds and related levies until paid, as well as special assessments, parcel taxes, and previously levied unpaid parcel taxes notwithstanding dissolution.

headings.title: Assignment to common road districts and allocation of remaining funds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Assigns dissolved district land to new or existing chapter 231 common road districts, allocates post-debt remaining funds proportionately by assigned acreage, and allocates subsequently paid parcel-specific funds (other than subsection 5 bond funds) to the common road district containing those parcels.

Checked "in lieu of section 233.290 or 233.295" scope limited to fourth-classification counties, 50-voter petition, four-year waiting period, archived wording duplication in subsection 2 ("make an order that the dissolution of the special road district order that the question..."), ballot form, majority disincorporation, preservation of bonds/levies/parcel assessments, and chapter 231 common-road-district assignment and fund allocation. Retained all six titles as accurate.

headings.title: Eligible counties and preservation of existing rights and obligations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1992 H.B. 1240 § 1; catchline parenthetically notes Cass and Platte counties). Authorizes special road district boundary changes in counties under 100,000 inhabitants containing all or part of a city of 350,000 or more, and specifies that boundary changes do not impair district organization, property rights, privileges, contracts, obligations, liens, or charges.

headings.title: Adjacent landowner petition for inclusion in district
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Permits 50% of owners of adjacent territory or tracts who own at least 50% of its real estate to file a written inclusion petition with the district commissioners describing the property, constituting petitioners' assent to inclusion.

headings.title: Published notice, show-cause hearing, and implied assent
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires the board clerk or secretary to publish newspaper notice of the petition and show-cause hearing, directs the board to hear the petition and written objections (with adjournment authority), and treats failure to show written cause as assent to inclusion.

headings.title: Board decision criteria, circuit clerk filing, and county approval
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Directs the board to grant the petition if in the district's best interest, or deny it if part cannot practically be served or should be excluded; requires filing a granting order with the circuit clerk and makes finality contingent on county governing body approval.

headings.title: Road maintenance duty and district taxation of added territory
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Requires the special road district to maintain public roads in included territory like its other roads and subjects included territory to district property taxes.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived version (5 subsections) and history note (L. 1992 H.B. 1240 § 1); verified source identity and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Checked statutory population bracket (<100,000 containing all or part of a >= 350,000 city) versus catchline parenthetical naming of Cass and Platte counties, preservation of existing rights and obligations, 50%-owner/50%-real-estate adjacent inclusion petition, newspaper notice and implied assent, board decision criteria, circuit clerk filing, county governing body approval condition for finality, and road maintenance and district taxation of added territory. headings.title: Election extension option for fourth-classification counties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2008 S.B. 896). Authorizes extending a sections 233.170 to 233.315 road district by election in addition to other legal mechanisms, restricted solely to special road districts in fourth-classification counties. Revised title during review from "alternative" to "option" to reflect "in addition to" (cf. "in lieu of" in sections 233.177 and 233.297).

headings.title: Voter petition and county commission extension election order
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires the county commission, upon petition of at least 35 registered voters in the existing district and the lesser of 35 or 50% of registered voters in the added area, to enter an order of record submitting the proposed extension (with title, approval date, and proposed boundaries) to voters of the proposed district.

headings.title: Ballot form for special road district extension
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 (including indented ballot block) and history note. Sets the substantial ballot question form for extending a special road district under this section.

headings.title: Effect of vote and ten-day effective date for orders
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Directs county commission orders declaring the vote result and expanding the district upon majority approval, leaves territory unchanged upon majority rejection, and makes any order under this section effective ten days after entry.

headings.title: Applicability to counties operating under township organization
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 8836). Governs organizing a special road district within one or more incorporated townships in counties operating under township organization.

headings.title: District division, corporate status, naming, and general powers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Directs the county commission to divide county territory into road districts under sections 233.320 to 233.445 and establishes each district as a public body corporate with naming, litigation, property-holding, and contracting powers.

headings.title: Territory size, contiguity requirements, and large-city exclusion
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Permits any advisable dimensions wholly within the organizing county with at least 640 contiguous acres, while prohibiting division of territory within corporate limits of a city of 150,000 population.

Checked township-organization county applicability (contrasted with section 233.170), county commission district division under sections 233.320 to 233.445, public body corporate status and powers, single-county and 640-contiguous-acre requirements, and 150,000-population city exclusion. headings.title: Resident-landowner petition filing and clerk notice requirements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 8837). Covers petitions signed by owners of a majority of acres owned by county residents residing in the proposed sections 233.320 to 233.445 district, filing thirty days before the next regular county commission term, and clerk notice by three weekly newspaper publications or five public handbills notifying resident landowners of the hearing and remonstrance deadline.

headings.title: Written resident-landowner remonstrances against district formation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Permits resident landowners in the proposed district to file joint or separate written remonstrances stating specific, separate objections with the county clerk on or before the first day of the regular term.

headings.title: Hearing, boundary changes, and incorporation order
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Directs the county commission to hear the petition and remonstrances, permits public-good boundary adjustments, and requires an incorporation order setting established boundaries if owners of a majority of resident-owned acres consent after boundary changes.

headings.title: Incorporation upon unopposed or amended petitions and notice safeguard
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history notes. Covers verifying majority resident-owned acreage when no remonstrance is filed or all are overruled, incorporating per original or amended petitions filed prior to the order, and prohibiting addition of unnotified land without owner written consent or open-meeting hearing notice and opportunity to remonstrate.

headings.title: Political subdivision status upon incorporation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history notes. Declares an incorporated public road district to be a political subdivision of the state for governmental purposes under the order's name with all statutory powers.

headings.title: Initial commissioner appointments and staggered annual elections
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 8838, A.L. 1978 H.B. 971). Directs county commission appointment of three initial commissioners (district voters) until the second Tuesday in April, followed by voter election of three staggered-term commissioners and annual municipal-election replacement for three-year terms.

headings.title: Voter qualification, unexpired-term vacancies, and oath
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Limits commissioners to district voters, directs remaining commissioners to fill unexpired vacancies caused by resignation, death, removal from the district, or sale of all land owned in the district (retaining archived source phrasing), and requires filing the constitutional and statutory oath with the county clerk.

headings.title: County commission election call after board failure
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Authorizes and requires the county commission to call an election to fill term-expiration vacancies if the board of commissioners fails to call an annual election.

Checked initial appointments and staggered municipal elections, district-voter qualification alongside archived "sale of all land owned by him in the district" vacancy trigger, remaining-commissioner vacancy filling, oath filing, and county commission duty to call an election after board failure (contrasted with appointment power in section 233.180(3)). headings.title: Organizational meeting, officer elections, and subsequent meetings
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 8839). Requires appointed and qualified commissioners to meet in the district and elect a president, vice president, and secretary (allowing a nonmember secretary by unanimous vote), and provides for subsequent meetings as agreed in writing or ordered by the president or vice president.

headings.title: District treasurer appointment, double bond, and liability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Directs commissioners to appoint a board treasurer who must give a board-approved bond in double the likely moneys (payable to the district and filed with the board secretary) and be responsible on the bond for all moneys deposited under sections 233.320 to 233.445.

headings.title: Duties of board president and vice president
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Covers the president's duties (presiding at meetings, signing minutes, records, and warrants, supervising work, and performing board-empowered or statutory acts) and the vice president acting during the president's absence from the county or a board meeting.

headings.title: Secretary recordkeeping and attestation duties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history notes. Requires the secretary to keep a true record of drawn warrants and written district contracts, attest warrants and contracts, keep board meeting minutes, and perform other legally required duties.

headings.title: Credit of funds and warrant signing requirements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history notes. Requires all money paid to the district treasurer to be credited to the district and paid out only on warrants signed by the president or vice president and attested by the secretary unless otherwise authorized by law.

headings.title: Township delivery and use of former districts' tools and machinery
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/effective-date notes (RSMo 1939 § 8840, A.L. 1990 S.B. 479 & 649, effective 5-30-90). Requires the township board of trustees, upon commissioner organization, to deliver road tools and machinery of former merged districts to the commissioners against receipt for road and bridge work.

headings.title: Township treasurer transfer of merged district funds upon demand
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Requires township boards to cause the township treasurer to pay over to the special road district treasurer all moneys belonging to merged districts upon demand of the special road district board.

headings.title: Commissioners' highway control, maintenance powers, and contracting
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Grants commissioners (subject to subsection 4) exclusive jurisdiction over non-state public highways, bridges, and culverts in the district with road-overseer powers, maintenance duties within available means, hiring and equipment acquisition powers, and contracting authority.

headings.title: Concurrent jurisdiction and equipment contracts with special road subdistricts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes (effective 5-30-90). Grants sections 233.500 to 233.520 special road subdistricts concurrent jurisdiction over non-state public highways, bridges, and culverts within subdistrict boundaries with any overlapping special road district and permits contracts to use subsection 1 tools and machinery.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived version (4 subsections) and history/effective-date notes (RSMo 1939 § 8840, A.L. 1990 S.B. 479 & 649, effective 5-30-90); verified source identity and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Checked township board tool delivery, township treasurer fund transfer upon board demand, sole non-state highway control subject to subsection 4, maintenance/equipment/contracting powers, and concurrent jurisdiction and equipment contracts with sections 233.500 to 233.520 special road subdistricts. headings.title: Road and bridge bond authority, debt limit, and terms
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 8843 through A.L. 1990 H.B. 1621). Authorizes township-county special road district commissioners to issue tax-payable road and bridge bonds up to 5% of assessed valuation (including existing tax-payable debt) in $100-multiple denominations at legally permitted interest rates maturing within 20 years.

headings.title: Submitting bond question to voters and election notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Requires the board of commissioners, when proposing bonds, to order submission of the question to district voters with an election notice stating the bond amount.

headings.title: Recording results and voter-approved bond execution and levy
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Requires recording the election result and, upon approval by the constitutionally required voter percentage, directs execution of the bonds and levy and collection of a direct annual property tax sufficient for principal and interest as due. Revised title during review to preserve voter-approval condition.

headings.title: Ballot form for special road district bonds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 (including indented ballot block) and history notes. Sets the substantial ballot question form for submitting special road district bonds.

headings.title: Minimum sale price, warrant disbursement, and permitted uses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history notes. Prohibits selling bonds below 95% of par value (retaining archived source typo "less then"), directs payment of proceeds to the district treasurer for warrant disbursement signed by the president or vice president and attested by the secretary, and restricts proceeds to election costs and district bridge, culvert, and road work.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived version (5 subsections, including indented ballot form) and history/prior-revision notes (RSMo 1939 § 8843 through A.L. 1990 H.B. 1621); verified source identity and all SHA-256 fingerprints. headings.title: Resident-landowner improvement petition, plans, and state engineer review
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 8844). Covers permanent road improvement petitions signed by owners of a majority of resident-owned acres within one-half mile (stating endpoints, improvement type, and up to 15 installments), commissioners' preparation of map, profile, plans, specifications, and estimate, and state highway engineer approval or revision.

headings.title: Land valuation and distance classifications
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Requires commissioners to fix fair, impartial valuations on each tract independent of buildings and prepare a land list classifying tracts by distance bands (within 0.5, 0.5–1, 1–1.5, and over 1.5 miles from the road).

headings.title: Averaging commissioner valuations upon disagreement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Directs commissioners, if unable to agree on a tract's valuation, to sum each commissioner's independent-of-buildings valuation and divide by three.

headings.title: Certification, county clerk filing, hearing notice, and rescheduling
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history notes. Covers certifying and acknowledging the land list like deeds, filing the petition, list, map, profile, plans, specifications, and estimate with the county clerk, publishing at least two weekly notices of the county commission hearing at least two weeks out (retaining archived phrasing "valuation of therein indicated"), and issuing new notice if the commission is not in session.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived version (4 subsections) and history/prior-revision notes (RSMo 1939 § 8844); verified source identity and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Checked resident-landowner one-half-mile petition, plans/profile/estimate and state highway engineer review, tract valuations independent of buildings and four distance bands, 3-commissioner tie-breaking average, acknowledged certification, county clerk filing, two-week newspaper notice, rescheduling if commission is not in session, and archived phrasing "valuation of therein indicated" in subsection 4. headings.title: Filing written landowner protests and objections before hearing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 8845). Permits landowners within one-half mile of the road in a township-county special road district to file signed written protests describing their land and acreage before the noticed hearing day, and permits anyone interested in district land to show why the road cannot be improved and charged against district lands.

headings.title: County commission consideration and prima facie petition effect
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 8845). Directs the county commission in township-county road improvement proceedings to consider the petition, filed protests, and reasons against the improvement on or after the noticed day, making the petition prima facie evidence of its allegations.

headings.title: Petition dismissal or hearing on land-list and valuation objections
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Directs dismissal if owners of a majority of resident-owned acres within one-half mile protest or sufficient bar is shown (unlike section 233.210(3), without a cost-judgment clause here); otherwise, upon verifying lawful road establishment and sections 233.320 to 233.445 clerk notice, requires hearing land-list and valuation objections with authority to continue.

headings.title: Valuation approval, cost findings, special tax order, and installments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history notes. Covers altering and approving the land list and valuations with clerk certification, finding estimated improvement, preparatory, petitioner attorney's fee, and incidental costs, ordering a special tax for the aggregate plus 10% for emergencies, ordering the improvement per filed plans, and stating the petitioned installment count.

headings.title: Single-installment special tax bills and required contents
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 8847). Requires the county clerk, when a special tax is ordered payable in one installment, to issue a separate numbered special tax bill per tract in favor of the district stating order date, tract description, and assessed amount, signed by the district president or vice president and attested by the clerk.

headings.title: Record book, deposit with district treasurer, and publication notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Requires the county clerk to record tax-bill abstracts, deposit the bills with the district treasurer, and publish one newspaper notice of issuance and delivery (retaining archived source phrasing "order to the county commission").

headings.title: Tax-bill lien priority and delinquency interest
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Makes each tax bill a paramount lien (except general state, county, school, and road taxes) covering collection costs and commission-fixed attorney's fees, and imposes 8% annual interest on bills unpaid thirty days after the order date.

headings.title: District treasurer payment collection, cancellation, and clerk notation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history notes. Requires the district treasurer to receive and record payments, cancel paid tax bills, and credit principal and interest on a special district account, and requires the county clerk to note payment in the record book upon exhibition or report.

headings.title: Commissioner borrowing against unpaid single-installment tax bills
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history notes. Authorizes commissioners after thirty days to borrow up to the unpaid tax-bill total at up to 8% interest, deposited with the district treasurer and repayable solely via warrants from collections of those unpaid bills with no other district or commissioner obligation.

headings.title: Lien foreclosure suits, prima facie evidence, and attorney's fees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history notes. Permits circuit court foreclosure suits after six months unpaid and requires them after twelve months with the district as plaintiff, makes each tax bill prima facie evidence of a valid lien, and taxes a court-fixed reasonable attorney's fee as costs.

headings.title: Restricted uses of tax-bill collections, borrowed funds, and interest
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history notes. Restricts tax-bill collections, borrowed funds, and depositary interest (drawn by warrants) to preparatory costs, petitioner attorney's fees, road improvement per filed plans, working/administrative/incidental expenses, and remaining balance for maintenance, subject to repaying borrowed money with interest from unpaid bill collections.

headings.title: Equal multi-installment schedule and interest apportionment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 8848). Provides that when a special tax order recites a petition for more than one installment, the tax is payable in the petitioned number of equal installments (not exceeding fifteen) with interest apportioned against district lands by the same rule as principal.

headings.title: Installment due dates and six percent interest calculation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (including subdivisions (1)–(2)) and history notes. Sets December 31 annual installment due dates and 6% annual interest accrual periods (to April 1) depending on whether the order is entered January 1–October 31 or on or after November 1.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived version (2 subsections, including subdivisions (1)–(2)) and history/prior-revision notes (RSMo 1939 § 8848); verified source identity and all SHA-256 fingerprints. headings.title: County clerk special tax record book entries
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 8848). Directs the county clerk after the assessment order to procure a special tax record book and enter each tract's special tax, interest charges, installment dates, and amounts.

headings.title: Installment tax bill issuance, lien priority, and monthly penalties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Requires delivering separate installment special tax bills to the county collector at least thirty days before due dates, specifies bill contents, creates a paramount lien (except general taxes) including a court-fixed reasonable attorney's fee (cf. section 233.235(2) "county commission"), and adds 2% delinquency penalty plus 2% monthly until paid.

headings.title: County collector payment receipts, cancellation, and clerk notation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Directs the county collector to receive and record payments and cancel paid tax bills, and requires the county clerk to note payment in the special tax record book upon exhibition or collector report.

headings.title: Remittance to district treasurer and special district accounting
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history notes. Requires the county collector to pay all tax-bill collections to the special road district treasurer, who must credit the district on a special account distinguishing principal from interest and penalties.

headings.title: Bond issuance limit, terms, installments, and place of payment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 8848). Requires township-county road district commissioners after the assessment order to issue special assessment bonds up to 90% of the ordered tax in minimum $100 denominations at up to 6% interest payable April 1 and October 1, maturing April 1 in the same number of (not necessarily equal) installments as the tax at a named bank or trust company.

headings.title: Execution, registration, district treasurer custody, and investment eligibility
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Covers execution by the district president, county clerk attestation/registration, state auditor registration, deposit with the district treasurer under sections 233.320 to 233.445, lawful security eligibility referencing sections 242.010 to 242.690, 243.010 to 243.540, and 108.240 to 108.300 (retaining archived phrasing "eligible and by sections"), and county commission school/trust fund investment at par.

headings.title: Public or private bond sale and minimum price
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 8848). Authorizes special road district commissioners to sell special assessment bonds at public or private sale for not less than 95% of face value.

headings.title: Payment sources, interest reserve requirement, and bond payment duty
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Limits bond collectibility to special tax bills, bond sales, and depositary interest; requires the district treasurer to reserve funds for interest due before the next tax installment plus 3% of unmatured bond principal; and directs application of applicable funds to due and unpaid bonds and interest.

headings.title: Dedicated tax-bill use for bonds and surplus exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Dedicates special tax-bill collections to bond principal and interest while allowing surplus above past-due bonds, upcoming bonds/interest before the next installment, and a 3% unmatured-principal reserve to be used for other authorized purposes (retaining archived source phrasing "except that money may be collected... may").

headings.title: Bond delivery upon sale and cancellation upon payment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history notes. Requires the district treasurer to deliver sold bonds upon commissioners' order and receipt of payment, and to cancel paid bonds and deliver them to the county clerk.

headings.title: Permitted uses of bond proceeds, surplus collections, and interest
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history notes. Restricts unreserved bond proceeds, authorized surplus tax-bill collections, and excess depositary interest (drawn by warrants) to preparatory costs, petitioner attorney's fees, road improvement per filed plans, working/administrative/incidental expenses, and remaining balance for maintenance.

headings.title: Partial payments without cancellation until paid in full
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 8849). Authorizes district treasurers and collectors to receive and receipt for partial payments of special tax bills without cancelling any bill until paid in full.

headings.title: Tax apportionment and separate bills for divided tracts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Directs the county commission, upon an owner's application when a taxed tract is or will be divided, to apportion the special tax across the resulting tracts for separate subsequent tax bills.

headings.title: Validity of tax bills with errors and clerk corrections
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Preserves the validity of sections 233.320 to 233.445 special tax bills despite errors to the proper amount and extent, and empowers the county clerk to correct errors at any time.

headings.title: Written contract with lowest and best bidder, penalties, and bond
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 8850). Directs district commissioners after an improvement order to enter a written contract with the lowest and best bidder containing a completion deadline, daily delay penalty, and approved contractor performance and labor/material payment bond. Revised title during review to restore exact statutory phrasing "lowest and best bidder".

headings.title: Bid advertising and commissioner conflict-of-interest prohibition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Allows commissioners to advertise for bids as they choose and prohibits letting the contract to a commissioner or allowing a commissioner any direct or indirect pecuniary interest beyond official duties.

headings.title: Contract price cap and eighty percent progress-payment limit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Caps contract payment at the commission's found estimated cost plus 10%, and bars paying more than 80% of the value of work performed and materials furnished prior to entire completion.

headings.title: Warrants on district treasurer for contractor payments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history notes. Directs commissioners to draw warrants on the district treasurer as contractor payments become payable under the contract.

Revised subsection 1 title to restore exact statutory phrasing "lowest and best bidder"; retained subsections 2–4.

headings.title: Township or county collector compensation for special tax bills
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 8854). Provides township or county collectors the same compensation for collecting sections 233.320 to 233.445 special tax bills as if collected as county taxes.

headings.title: County clerk fees for tax bills, records, and bonds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Sets itemized county clerk fees under sections 233.320 to 233.445 (6 cents per tax bill issued/attested, 5 cents per recorded abstract, 4 cents per tract for installment tax records, 20 cents per bond attested/registered, and statutory or commission-fixed pay for other services).

headings.title: Unpaid commissioner service and district expense reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Provides that commissioners of sections 233.320 to 233.445 districts receive no compensation for services, while requiring reimbursement of all district business expenses including reasonable attorney's fees.

headings.title: Disincorporation by resident-landowner acreage petition, notice, and hearing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 8855 through A.L. 2025 H.B. 199). Authorizes a county commission, upon petition of owners of a majority of resident-owned acres in a sections 233.320 to 233.445 district and four successive weeks' published newspaper notice before hearing, to disincorporate the district if it finds the public good advanced.

headings.title: Qualifying-county November 2026 dissolution ballot and approved transfer
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes (A.L. 2025 H.B. 199; catchline parenthetically references Bates County). For any special road district in a county with 15,700–17,600 inhabitants and a county seat with 4,210–6,000 inhabitants, requires placing dissolution on the ballot no later than the November 2026 general election and transfers district responsibilities and outstanding obligations to the county if voters approve; describes archived text neutrally without asserting post-election status. Revised title during review to reflect voter-approval condition on transfer.

headings.title: Calling special road district or township bond elections
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 8610, A.L. 1978 H.B. 971). Requires a special road district board proposing road bonds to order voter submission, and requires the county commission to order voter submission for township road bonds upon written petition of twenty township voters.

headings.title: Election notice stating bond amount
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Requires the bond election notice in either a special road district or township election to state the amount of bonds to be issued.

headings.title: Recording results, bond execution, and tax levy on two-thirds vote
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Requires entering results on the board or county commission records and, upon approval by two-thirds of voters voting on the question, directs bond execution and levy and collection of a direct annual property tax in the district or township for principal and interest. Revised title during review to preserve the two-thirds approval condition on bond execution and levy.

headings.title: Annual certification of road district bond debt requirements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history notes. Requires the road district board clerk by May 1 each year (or the state auditor immediately thereafter upon clerk default) to certify to the county commission(s) the amount needed for bond interest and maturing principal in the next year.

headings.title: Levying, extending, and collecting road district bond taxes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history notes. Directs county commissions upon receiving the subsection 4 certificate to levy the required road district tax rate at regular levy time, clerks to extend it on tax books, and collectors to collect it like general taxes.

headings.title: Levying, extending, and collecting township bond taxes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history notes. Covers determining, ordering, and levying the annual tax rate on taxable property in townships with outstanding bonds under this section at regular levy time, extending the rate on tax books by the county clerk, and collection by the collector like general taxes (retaining archived source text's omitted main verb clause in the first sentence without silent repair).

headings.title: Applicability of state tax collection laws and remedies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history notes. Makes all Missouri laws, rights, and remedies for collecting state, county, school, and other taxes applicable to taxes authorized under this section.

headings.title: Creation of special road subdistricts and corporate powers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/effective-date notes (L. 1990 S.B. 479 & 649 § 1, effective 5-30-90). Authorizes county commissions to create special road subdistricts under sections 233.500 to 233.520 within a section 233.015, 233.170, or 233.320 special road district or in county areas outside any special road district, conferring public body corporate status, naming, litigation, property, and contracting powers.

headings.title: Minimum road length, adjacent territory, and assessed valuation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Requires a special road subdistrict to include a public road of at least one mile, adjacent lands and roads of at least one-fourth mile on either side, and an assessed valuation of at least $1 million per the latest state tax commission report.

headings.title: Landowner petition filing and clerk notice requirements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/effective-date notes (L. 1990 S.B. 479 & 649 § 2, effective 5-30-90). Covers petitions by a majority of landowners in a proposed sections 233.500 to 233.520 subdistrict filed thirty days before a county commission meeting, and clerk notice via three weekly newspaper publications and five public handbills notifying resident landowners of the hearing and remonstrance opportunity.

headings.title: Written resident-landowner remonstrances against subdistrict formation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Allows resident landowners within the proposed subdistrict to file joint or separate written remonstrances stating specific, separate objections with the county clerk on or before the county commission meeting.

headings.title: Hearing, boundary changes, and incorporation order
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Directs the county commission to hear the petition and remonstrances, permits public-good boundary adjustments, and requires an incorporation order setting established boundaries if a majority of resident landowners in the changed subdistrict signed or consented in writing.

headings.title: Incorporation upon unopposed or amended petitions and notice safeguard
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Directs verifying majority landowner signatures when remonstrances are absent or overruled, incorporating under the original or amended petition filed before the order, and prohibiting inclusion of unnotified land without written owner consent or open-meeting hearing notice and opportunity to remonstrate.

headings.title: Political subdivision status upon incorporation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and notes. Declares an incorporated special road subdistrict to be a political subdivision of the state for governmental purposes under the order's name with all sections 233.500 to 233.520 powers.

headings.title: Initial subdistrict commissioner appointments and staggered annual elections
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/effective-date notes (L. 1990 S.B. 479 & 649 § 3, effective 5-30-90). Directs county commission appointment of three initial subdistrict commissioners (subdistrict voters) until the second Tuesday in April, followed by voter election of three staggered-term commissioners and annual municipal-election replacement for three-year terms.

headings.title: Voter qualification, unexpired-term vacancies, and oath
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Limits commissioners to subdistrict voters, directs remaining commissioners to fill unexpired vacancies caused by resignation, death, removal, or sale of all land owned in the subdistrict, and requires filing the constitutional and statutory oath with the county clerk.

headings.title: County commission election call after board failure
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Authorizes and requires the county commission to call an election to fill term-expiration vacancies if the subdistrict board fails to call an annual election.

headings.title: Organizational meeting and election of board officers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/effective-date notes (L. 1990 S.B. 479 & 649 § 4, effective 5-30-90). Requires appointed and qualified subdistrict commissioners to meet in the subdistrict and elect a president, vice president, and secretary, permitting a nonmember secretary by unanimous board vote.

headings.title: Meetings, county treasurer role, and president and vice president duties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Covers subsequent meetings, designating the county treasurer as board treasurer (responsible on official bond under sections 233.500 to 233.520), the president's presiding, signing, and supervisory duties, and the vice president acting during the president's absence.

headings.title: Secretary duties and warrant signing requirements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Covers the secretary's warrant/contract records, attestation, and minute-keeping duties, and requires county treasurer payouts of subdistrict funds to be made only on warrants signed by the president or vice president and attested by the secretary unless otherwise authorized by law.

headings.title: Authorized subdistrict tax, four-sevenths vote, and ballot form
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (including embedded HTML ballot table with FOR/AGAINST checkboxes) and history/effective-date notes (L. 1990 S.B. 479 & 649 § 5, effective 5-30-90). Authorizes a subdistrict property tax (including for section 233.513 bonds) contingent on four-sevenths voter approval at specified elections, sets the separate ballot form, and states levy versus non-levy outcomes.

headings.title: Tax levy, collection, county treasurer deposit, and warrant disbursement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Provides that approved subdistrict taxes are levied and collected like special road district taxes, deposited with the county treasurer, and disbursed only to the subdistrict president or vice president on signed, secretary-attested warrants.

headings.title: Subdistrict bond authority, limits, interest rates, and voter submission
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/effective-date notes (L. 1990 S.B. 479 & 649 § 6, effective 5-30-90). Authorizes subdistrict commissioners to issue tax-payable road and bridge bonds up to 5% of assessed valuation (including existing tax-payable debt) in $100-multiple denominations, allows commissioner-set semiannual interest rates notwithstanding section 108.180, caps maturity at 20 years, and requires voter submission.

headings.title: Election notice stating bond amount
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Requires the subdistrict bond election notice to state the amount of bonds to be issued.

headings.title: Ballot form for subdistrict road and bridge bonds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 (including embedded HTML ballot table with YES/NO checkboxes) and notes. Sets the substantial ballot question form for subdistrict road and bridge bonds.

headings.title: Recording results and bond execution upon four-sevenths vote
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Requires entering the vote result on subdistrict records and directs commissioners to order execution of the bonds if four-sevenths of voters voting on the question approve.

headings.title: Minimum sale price, warrant disbursement, and permitted bond uses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and notes. Bars selling bonds below 95% of par value, requires county treasurer deposit and signed/attested warrant disbursement, and restricts proceeds to election costs, subdistrict bridges/culverts, paving/surfacing new roads, and working/repairing/maintaining/dragging public roads.

headings.title: Payment sources, interest reserve requirement, and bond payment duty
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and notes. Limits bond collectibility to special tax bills, bond sales, and county depositary interest (retaining archived source text combining tax-supported bond authority in subsection 1 with special tax-bill repayment provisions in subsections 6–9); requires a county treasurer interest reserve plus 3% of unmatured principal and directs application of applicable funds to due bonds and interest.

headings.title: Dedicated tax-bill use for bonds and surplus exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and notes. Dedicates special tax-bill collections to paying bonds and interest, permitting surplus above past-due bonds, upcoming bonds/interest before the next installment, and a 3% unmatured-principal reserve to be used for other authorized purposes.

headings.title: Bond delivery upon sale and cancellation upon payment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and notes. Directs the county treasurer to deliver sold bonds to purchasers upon commissioners' order and receipt of payment, and to cancel paid bonds and deliver them to the county clerk.

headings.title: Permitted uses of bond proceeds, tax-bill collections, and interest
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and notes. Restricts unreserved bond-sale proceeds, special tax-bill collections (omitting the surplus-only qualifier found in sections 233.255(5) and 233.395(5)), and excess depositary interest (drawn by warrants) to preparatory costs, petitioner attorney's fees (retaining archived spelling "attorneys fee"), road improvement per filed plans, working/administrative/incidental expenses, and remaining balance for maintenance.

headings.title: Written contract, transportation department letting, penalties, and bond
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/effective-date notes (L. 1990 S.B. 479 & 649 § 7, effective 5-30-90). Requires subdistrict commissioners after an improvement order to enter a written contract with the lowest and best bidder in the same manner as the letting of public works contracts by the department of transportation, with completion deadline, daily delay penalty, and approved performance and labor/material payment bond. Revised title during review for clearer transportation-department letting phrasing aligned with subsection 2.

headings.title: Transportation department bid letting and commissioner conflict-of-interest bar
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Requires advertising and letting bids in the same manner as department of transportation public works contracts, and bars letting contracts to or permitting direct or indirect pecuniary interest by any subdistrict commissioner beyond sections 233.500 to 233.520 official duties.

headings.title: Contract price cap and eighty percent progress-payment limit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Caps contract payment at the county commission's found estimated cost plus 10%, and bars paying over 80% of the value of work actually performed and materials furnished until entire completion.

headings.title: Warrants on county treasurer for contractor payments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Directs subdistrict commissioners to draw warrants on the county treasurer as contractor payments become payable under contract terms.

headings.title: Disincorporation by landowner petition, notice, and hearing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/effective-date notes (L. 1990 S.B. 479 & 649 § 8, effective 5-30-90). Authorizes the county commission, upon petition of a majority of landowners in a sections 233.500 to 233.520 subdistrict and four successive weeks' published newspaper notice before hearing, to disincorporate the subdistrict if it finds the public good advanced.

headings.title: Preservation of existing rights and contracts upon dissolution
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Provides that subdistrict dissolution does not invalidate or affect any right accruing to the subdistrict or any person, or any contract entered into by or imposed on the subdistrict.

headings.title: Appointment, oath, and bond of dissolution trustee
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Requires the county commission upon dissolving a subdistrict to appoint a competent trustee, who must take an oath and give a commission-approved bond with sufficient security before entering upon duties.

headings.title: Trustee powers to litigate, liquidate, and wind up affairs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Empowers the trustee, under county commission order and direction, to prosecute and defend suits, collect moneys due, liquidate lawful demands, sell necessary subdistrict property, and exercise statutory subdistrict powers to close affairs.

headings.title: Final remittance of remaining funds and delivery of records
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and notes. Requires the trustee, after closing affairs and paying all debts, to pay remaining funds to the county treasurer against receipt and deliver all books, papers, records, and deeds to the county clerk.
